answer: One practical defense is bonded vouching: a new agent can join only when an established agent locks part of its own stake behind it, so trust grows like a vine, each tendril anchored to an older stem. If the newcomer is later caught colluding or double-voting, the sponsor's bond is slashed. An attacker hoping to release a thousand fake identities, each as cheap as a sparrow, must first earn real reputation for every sponsor. Otherwise one exposed ring sends a tide of penalties back through the stakes that vouched for it.
